title: Escrow, Title & Closing Procedures
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: A preliminary title report is best understood as:
options: A guarantee that title has no issues
A document identifying proposed coverage, requirements, and exceptions
A legal opinion from the agent
rationales: A report may list matters requiring attention.
Correct. It identifies proposed coverage and matters relevant before a policy issues.
Agents should not provide title legal opinions.
Escrow instructions remain separate authority.

questions.stem: A buyer asks whether an easement means they can build a gate. The agent should:
options: Refer the question to title or qualified counsel
rationales: An unsupported promise can mislead.
Legal interpretation exceeds the ordinary agent role.
Correct. The agent can identify and route the issue without diagnosing legal rights.
The report should be reviewed.

questions.stem: A party calls escrow and verbally directs release of disputed funds. Escrow should act based on:
rationales: Volume is not authority.
Correct. Escrow operates under authorized instructions and applicable requirements.
An agent cannot substitute personal judgment for authority.
Price is unrelated.

options: Acceptance of an instrument for public county records
rationales: Signing is a different step.
Approval is not recording.
Correct. Recording concerns public county record entry.
Possession is separate.

options: Loan documents are ready; I will confirm remaining escrow, funding, and recording steps
Keys can be handed over now
Nothing can delay a funded loan
rationales: The agent cannot guarantee closing.
Correct. It communicates known facts without promising an outcome.
Possession must be authorized.
Other required steps may remain.

questions.stem: A seller's payoff exceeds projected proceeds. The agent should:
options: Use buyer deposit to cover it
Promptly escalate and let authorized parties determine a solution
Assure seller it does not matter
rationales: Buyer funds cannot be repurposed.
Correct. A shortfall requires prompt broker and escrow coordination, not an agent-created solution.
It may prevent closing.
An agent cannot alter authorized settlement information.

questions.stem: The proper agent role in title review is to:
options: Identify questions and route them to qualified professionals
rationales: Legal conclusions may exceed license scope.
Correct. Agents surface issues and coordinate qualified review.
Agents cannot guarantee a title product.
Exceptions are addressed through authorized processes.

questions.stem: A buyer wants keys before recording is confirmed. The best next step is to:
options: Give keys because movers are waiting
Confirm written authority, escrow status, and broker procedure first
rationales: Convenience is not authority.
Correct. Early access creates risk and requires verified authority.
A neighbor cannot authorize possession.
The agent cannot guarantee recording.
Marketing is unrelated.
Correct. Vesting identifies the manner legal title is held.
Rate locks are loan matters.
Inspection is separate.

questions.stem: Which buyer information is usually unnecessary in a factual status update to a seller?
options: That an extension request was sent
rationales: Factual status may be relevant.
A schedule status can be relevant.
Correct. Full tax returns are private and normally unnecessary.
The request's existence may be relevant.

questions.stem: A contingency should be marked removed when:
options: Applicable written action supports that status
rationales: Optimism is not evidence.
Correct. Use the applicable written transaction evidence.
Positive conversation may not remove a contingency.
A request does not change a contract.

options: Always a defect that kills the sale
A stated matter outside or limited under coverage
rationales: Its effect must be evaluated, not assumed.
Correct. Exceptions identify matters outside or limited under stated coverage.
Commission is separate.
Loans are separate.

questions.stem: Why keep a detailed post-close file?
options: To answer later questions with a factual record
rationales: A file should be preserved under policy.
Correct. Later questions may arise about disclosures, payments, possession, or recording.
Authorized client delivery remains important.
The file does not replace public title records.

options: A lender disbursing proceeds under its process
rationales: Recording is separate.
Correct. Funding is lender disbursement under its process.
Possession is separate.
Listing is unrelated.

questions.stem: A report names a seller whose name differs from the purchase agreement. The agent should:
options: Promptly flag it to title, broker, and appropriate parties
Assure buyer it is a typo
rationales: Name mismatch can affect authority or vesting.
Correct. Prompt verification prevents a late closing problem.
Only authorized professionals can correct title documents.
The agent should not assume the cause.

questions.stem: An agent's transaction milestone board should use:
options: Actual dates, responsible parties, and supporting evidence
rationales: Vagueness creates avoidable mistakes.
Correct. Specific milestones support clear coordination and review.
Memory is not a durable record.
Social messages are not a complete transaction system.
